svg.style: background: transparent; background-color: transparent; color-scheme: light dark;

g.text: AIMS on Luminate — target topology for the POC

Every solid arrow out of an AIMS component passes through the gateway — the only path on which policy, guardrails, audit, tracing and cost exist. A direct provider call is not "less governed", it is ungoverned.
Traffic leaves the AIMS estate to be governed and comes back into it — the gateway reaches the MCP servers on cluster-internal Service addresses, below the Okta hop (DD-4).

div.div:
Remediation Agent · aims-remediation
S4 — not registered until G4 (stop control) and G11 resolve

g.text: The dashed red hops are direct calls between agents, at their own service addresses. They do not pass
through Luminate and cannot today (G3). Each agent re-enters the gateway on its own identity for its own
egress, so governance is complete per hop and absent between hops.

g.text: No agent in the POC reaches the write server. The only path to infrastructure change is the S4 agent,
which does not exist yet. Each server keeps enforcing its own authorization internally — Luminate is an
additional layer, never a replacement for it.
